rationale: I read the full held EO 9811 (11 FR 14483, official FR text; neighbouring items ignored). Its single operative sentence extends trust or alienation-restriction periods expiring during calendar 1947 'for a further period of twenty-five years from the date on which any such trust would otherwise expire', excluding cases Congress reserved. The order acts once on a closed class and fixes its own duration, so the extensions it made ran out no later than the end of 1972; it contains no continuing command. I tried to refute the NO: any later continuation of particular trusts (later extension orders, departmental action under the authority delegated by EO 10250, or statutes extending trust periods indefinitely) would be a new act under other authority, not continued operation of EO 9811; the 1989 Codification line points to EO 10250 as a delegation lead, not to EO 9811 being in force. The held TERM record is from the official FR text, not the APP copy. Independent view NO (expired by own term); I agree, while recording that this is a 'spent by own term' NO rather than an express revocation and the exact last expiry and the EO 10250 delegation are lifecycle gaps. Nonauthoritative AI hypothesis.
